html:
The First Serbian Uprising was a revolt of Serbs against the Ottoman janissaries ruling the area of Belgrade, launched at Orašac on 14 February 1804 under Karađorđe, a livestock trader.

It began as a rising against janissary warlords who had killed Serbian notables, but grew into a war for independence. The rebels won battles, took Belgrade in 1806 and set up a council of state. Russia backed them while it was at war with the Ottomans, but when Russia made peace in 1812 to face Napoleon, the Ottomans crushed the uprising in 1813. Karađorđe fled. A second uprising in 1815 led to the autonomous Principality of Serbia, and Karađorđe's descendants became one of Serbia's two royal houses.
sum: The First Serbian Uprising was a revolt of Serbs against the Ottoman janissaries ruling the area of Belgrade, launched at Orašac on 14 February 1804 under Karađorđe, a livestock trader.
